translations.text: It is all the same to me whether or not I go into Leinster: their slaughters will be many; it is plain from their signs.
However they may be besides, their ring-forts will be empty; weak will be their power yonder on the Day of Judgement.
You think great the number of monks with Kevin himself, but two thirds are with Abban and with Moling of the mountain.
The third of their lay warriors whom they will not bring to heaven, it is they who will bring me the reward of my labour.
These are the lamps that will light up Leinster; I will now make their crosses over my face.
The fire will not burn [?] the hand of strong will [?]; heaven and earth will go to their monks.
Though they should take possession from the Bir to the Barrow, on every side they would go, demons would not assail them.
True will be this chant that the angels chant to me: the territories of this little body will be these, for my soul.
Chosen are these three whom we foretell: the gracious son Abban, who is [?] by us, Moling of the Taeidhen [?], and Kevin of the Glen.
Let their stories be written, let their [?] be feasts; sufferings did not disturb them, without benefit to their souls.
Every free man who [?] them in the midst of his land, except one of them, will not obtain grace, law or kingship.
Every one who is nearest to their mighty monastic cities, they will be the worst for you on the world of Banba.
Until this day comes, they will be empty and void, after the neglect of sovereignty, without mighty battles.
The Creator will apportion to them, into the midst of his temple, the sovereignty of the other world and the goodness of this world.
And the other clerics who will come from them here will be withered and bent; O woman, it is all the same. All the same.
